curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `h j k l`; counts; `0`, `^`, `$`, `g_`, `|`; `w W e E b B ge gE`; `gg`, `G`; `gj`, `gk`
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Reach characters, words, line boundaries, and buffer boundaries without editing
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Move to an identifier, last nonblank character, next WORD, or requested line; compare logical and wrapped display lines
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core. `gj/gk` behavior depends on wrapping, but the distinction is portable

lessons.title: Move without leaving home
lessons.objective: Use h, j, k, and l with counts to reach nearby characters and rows.

activities.title: Four keys cover four directions
activities.body: In Normal mode, `h` and `l` move left and right while `j` and `k` move down and up. A count repeats the motion without editing text.
activities.grammar: h ←   j ↓   k ↑   l →   ·   count + motion
activities.contrast: Movement changes the cursor position, not the buffer.

activities.title: Cross a small value grid
activities.instruction: Move right three columns, down two rows, left once, then up once.

commandGroups.explanation: Move three columns right.
Move down two logical lines while preserving the preferred column.
Move one character left.
Move one logical line up.

feedback.success: The cursor crossed the grid without an edit.
feedback.why: Counts applied to h and j, while h and k supplied single-step corrections.

provenance.languageRationale: Short aligned Python assignments make row and column changes easy to see.

activities.title: Reach the status name
activities.instruction: Move seven characters right to the `s` after the underscore.

commandGroups.explanation: Apply a count to the rightward motion.

hints: Count the columns from the first `s`.

feedback.success: Landed on the second half of the identifier.
feedback.why: A count compressed seven identical rightward motions into one command.

provenance.languageRationale: An underscored Python name provides a clear character target.

activities.title: Descend, then correct
activities.instruction: Move down two lines and then three characters left.

commandGroups.explanation: Descend two logical lines.
Correct three columns to the left.

hints: Use one count for each direction.

feedback.success: Reached the mode key.
feedback.why: Vertical movement preserved the column before the horizontal correction.

provenance.languageRationale: Compact TOML rows support predictable two-axis navigation.

activities.title: Return from the southeast corner
activities.instruction: Reach column three of the first row using counted home-row motions.

commandGroups.explanation: Climb three rows.
Move five columns left.

hints: Solve the vertical and horizontal distances separately.

feedback.success: Returned to the northwest row.
feedback.why: Counts made the rectangular route explicit and repeatable.

provenance.languageRationale: Equal-width labels create a neutral movement grid without language trivia.

lessons.title: Land on line landmarks
lessons.objective: Reach the start, first text, end, last nonblank, or requested column of a line.

activities.title: A line has several useful edges
activities.body: `0` reaches column zero, `^` reaches the first nonblank, `$` reaches the physical end, and `g_` reaches the last nonblank. A count followed by `|` targets a one-based column.
activities.grammar: 0 → column zero · ^ → first text · $ → final character · g_ → last text · count| → column
activities.contrast: On a line with trailing spaces, `$` and `g_` deliberately land in different places.

activities.title: Inspect every edge of one call
activities.instruction: Visit column zero, first text, physical end, last nonblank, and column twelve.

commandGroups.explanation: Go to absolute column zero.
Skip indentation to the first nonblank.
Reach the final trailing space.
Return to the last nonblank character.
Go to one-based column twelve.

feedback.success: Every line landmark was distinct.
feedback.why: The motions expressed intent directly, including the difference between physical and nonblank ends.

provenance.languageRationale: An indented JavaScript call with trailing spaces exposes every line landmark.

activities.title: Ignore trailing space
activities.instruction: Move directly to the closing parenthesis, not the spaces after it.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the last nonblank character.

hints: The physical line end is too far right.

feedback.success: Landed on the closing parenthesis.
feedback.why: g_ ignored the trailing whitespace while preserving the buffer.

provenance.languageRationale: A Python call ends with an obvious nonblank character before hidden trailing space.

activities.title: Compare both meaningful edges
activities.instruction: Visit the first nonblank, physical end, then last nonblank of the YAML row.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the first nonblank.
Reach the physical end.
Return to the last nonblank.

feedback.success: Separated indentation, content, and trailing space.
feedback.why: Each motion named a different boundary instead of counting manually.

provenance.languageRationale: Indented YAML naturally distinguishes first text from both kinds of line end.

activities.title: Land on a later row and column
activities.instruction: Use counted `g_` to reach the third row's last nonblank, then go to column eight.

commandGroups.explanation: Move to the third row and its last nonblank.
Target one-based column eight.

hints: A count on `g_` also chooses a later line.

feedback.success: Reached the requested row and column.
feedback.why: The first count selected a line-relative landmark; the second selected an absolute column.

provenance.languageRationale: Calls of different lengths prove that g_ follows content rather than a fixed column.

lessons.title: Choose a word boundary
lessons.objective: Distinguish punctuation-sensitive words from whitespace-delimited WORDs using w and W.

activities.title: Words notice punctuation; WORDs notice whitespace
activities.body: Lowercase `w` advances through keyword and punctuation groups. Uppercase `W` treats every nonblank run as one WORD.
activities.grammar: w → next word group · W → next whitespace-delimited WORD
activities.contrast: In `cache.old`, w can stop at the dot and at old; W treats the whole token as one unit.

activities.title: Cross a dotted assignment
activities.instruction: Watch lowercase w visit punctuation and uppercase W jump by whitespace.

commandGroups.explanation: Move from cache to the punctuation group.
Move from the dot to old.
Move to the equals punctuation group.
Jump by whitespace to loader.

feedback.success: Saw both boundary systems in one line.
feedback.why: w exposed punctuation groups; W ignored their internal structure.

provenance.languageRationale: A dotted JavaScript property clearly separates word and WORD boundaries.

activities.title: Count across a dotted name
activities.instruction: Use one counted word motion to reach the start of `profile`.

commandGroups.explanation: Advance through two word groups.

hints: The dot is its own word group.

feedback.success: Landed at the start of profile.
feedback.why: The count traversed the identifier and punctuation groups.

provenance.languageRationale: A dotted property chain gives stable small-word boundaries.

activities.title: Switch boundary systems
activities.instruction: Jump to `ready` with W, move down, then use two small-word motions.

commandGroups.explanation: Treat alpha-beta as one WORD and reach ready.
Move to the next logical line.
Advance from whitespace to waiting.

feedback.success: Changed boundary systems deliberately.
feedback.why: W ignored internal punctuation, while w followed smaller lexical groups.

provenance.languageRationale: Log-like tokens naturally contrast hyphen, underscore, and whitespace boundaries.

activities.title: Navigate a path-like token
activities.instruction: Use two small-word motions inside the path, then W to reach the status.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the slash punctuation group.
Reach api after the slash.
Treat the rest of the path as one WORD and reach status.

hints: Let lowercase w expose the slash and api.
Use uppercase W for the path token's whitespace boundary.

feedback.success: Traversed a mixed path and status line.
feedback.why: The chosen case controlled whether punctuation mattered.

provenance.languageRationale: A shell-style path token makes punctuation-aware navigation practical.

lessons.title: Reach word edges in either direction
lessons.objective: Use e/E, b/B, and ge/gE to target word starts and ends while moving forward or backward.

activities.title: Starts and ends are separate targets
activities.body: `e` and `E` move forward to word ends. `b` and `B` move backward to starts. `ge` and `gE` move backward to ends, with uppercase variants using WORD boundaries.
activities.grammar: e/E → forward end · b/B → backward start · ge/gE → backward end
activities.contrast: Choose the edge you need before choosing lowercase word or uppercase WORD granularity.

activities.title: Tour starts and ends
activities.instruction: Visit small-word and WORD ends, reverse to their starts, then inspect backward ends.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the end of alpha.
Reach the end of the first WORD.
Return to the start of beta.
Return to the start of the whole WORD.
Move to the line end for the reverse examples.
Move backward to the prior small-word end.
Move backward to the prior WORD end.

feedback.success: Visited starts and ends in both directions.
feedback.why: Direction, edge, and boundary size are independent choices in Vim's motion vocabulary.

provenance.languageRationale: Dotted and hyphenated identifiers expose both small-word and WORD edges.

activities.title: Compare e and E
activities.instruction: Reach the end of `api`, then the end of the whole path-like WORD.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the small-word end of api.
Reach the end of the whitespace-delimited path WORD.

hints: Lowercase stops before punctuation groups are exhausted.

feedback.success: Reached two different forward ends.
feedback.why: e observed punctuation; E continued to the WORD boundary.

provenance.languageRationale: A log-style route provides several punctuation boundaries inside one WORD.

activities.title: Reverse to two starts
activities.instruction: From the final word, move to the small-word start behind it, then the WORD start.

commandGroups.explanation: Move to the start of ready.
Move to the start of the previous WORD.

hints: Use lowercase for the nearby lexical start.
Then use uppercase for the prior WORD.

feedback.success: Reversed to both start types.
feedback.why: b and B share direction but use different boundary sizes.

provenance.languageRationale: The same path line supports a controlled reverse-boundary comparison.

activities.title: Reverse by word ends
activities.instruction: From the line end, use ge then gE to land at the previous WORD end.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the prior small-word end.
Reach the prior whitespace-delimited WORD end.

feedback.success: Reversed across two kinds of end boundary.
feedback.why: ge followed lexical punctuation; gE followed whitespace-delimited WORDs.

provenance.languageRationale: Mixed punctuation makes the reverse end targets visually distinct.

lessons.title: Travel by line number
lessons.objective: Use gg, G, and counted G to reach the first, last, or requested buffer line.

activities.title: The buffer has absolute destinations
activities.body: `gg` reaches the first line, `G` reaches the last line, and a count before `G` reaches that one-based line number. Each lands on the first nonblank character.
activities.grammar: gg → first line · G → last line · countG → requested line
activities.contrast: A count on G names a line; it does not mean repeat G several times.

activities.title: Visit top, bottom, and line three
activities.instruction: Jump to the first line, the last line, then line three.

commandGroups.explanation: Jump to the first line and its first nonblank.
Jump to the final line.
Jump to one-based line three.

feedback.success: Reached three absolute buffer destinations.
feedback.why: gg and G chose edges, while 3G named a line directly.

provenance.languageRationale: Indented YAML-like rows reveal first-nonblank landing behavior.

activities.title: Return to the first import
activities.instruction: Jump directly from the last row to the first buffer line.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the first line and its first nonblank.

feedback.success: Returned to the first import.
feedback.why: gg ignored the current distance and targeted the buffer boundary.

provenance.languageRationale: A short import list gives an obvious first-line destination.

activities.title: Jump to bottom, then line two
activities.instruction: Reach the last line with G, then address line two directly.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the final line.
Address one-based line two.

hints: Use uppercase G for both destinations.
The second command needs a line number.

feedback.success: Used both forms of G.
feedback.why: Bare G chose the buffer end; 2G treated the count as an address.

provenance.languageRationale: A short region list makes one-based line addressing easy to verify.

activities.title: Go straight to line four
activities.instruction: Address the fourth line without visiting intermediate rows.

commandGroups.explanation: Use the count as a one-based line address.

feedback.success: Reached line four directly.
feedback.why: Counted G expresses an absolute destination rather than a travel distance.

provenance.languageRationale: A neutral color list keeps attention on line numbering.

lessons.title: Move through wrapped display lines
lessons.objective: Distinguish logical-line j/k from display-line gj/gk when a long line wraps.

activities.title: A wrapped row is still one logical line
activities.body: `j` and `k` move between newline-separated logical lines. `gj` and `gk` move between the visible wrapped rows inside those lines.
activities.grammar: j/k → logical line · gj/gk → displayed row
activities.contrast: With wrapping off, the motions often look identical; wrapping makes their different destinations visible.

activities.title: Walk a wrapped token, then change lines
activities.instruction: Move down two display rows, back up one, then down one logical line.

commandGroups.explanation: Move down one wrapped display row.
Move down another displayed row without leaving the logical line.
Move back up one display row.
Move to the next newline-separated logical line.

feedback.success: Separated display-row movement from logical-line movement.
feedback.why: gj and gk stayed within one wrapped line; j crossed the actual newline.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior; visible destinations depend on the configured wrap width.

provenance.languageRationale: Long neutral tokens wrap at deterministic character boundaries without language-dependent word wrapping.

activities.title: Stay on the logical line
activities.instruction: Move down one visible row without crossing a newline.

commandGroups.explanation: Move to the next displayed row of the same line.

hints: Plain j would seek a newline.

feedback.success: Stayed inside one logical line.
feedback.why: gj followed the screen layout created by wrapping.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior; visible destinations depend on wrapping.

provenance.languageRationale: A long neutral token creates deterministic wrapping without spaces.

activities.title: Change movement scale
activities.instruction: Move up one displayed row, then down one logical line.

commandGroups.explanation: Move up one displayed row within the first logical line.
Cross the newline while keeping the preferred display column.

feedback.success: Changed from display rows to logical lines.
feedback.why: gk followed wrapping; j followed the buffer's newline structure.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior; visible destinations depend on wrapping.

provenance.languageRationale: Paired long tokens keep wrapped columns deterministic across both logical lines.

activities.title: Skip two display rows
activities.instruction: Use one counted display-line motion to reach the third visible row.

commandGroups.explanation: Move down two displayed rows while remaining on one logical line.

hints: Put the count before the complete g-prefixed motion.

feedback.success: Skipped two wrapped rows.
feedback.why: The count multiplied display-line movement, not logical-line movement.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior; visible destinations depend on wrapping.

provenance.languageRationale: A deterministic long token makes the two-row display jump measurable.

lessons.title: Choose the smallest useful motion
lessons.objective: Combine line, word, column, and buffer motions without changing text.

activities.title: Name the destination before the keys
activities.body: Efficient movement comes from recognizing the target: nearby character, word edge, line landmark, requested line, or wrapped display row.
activities.contrast: The shortest useful command is the one whose meaning matches the destination, not always the one with the fewest keys.

activities.title: Combine absolute and local movement
activities.instruction: Visit the first line's value, jump to the last line, normalize to first text, then address column six.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the first buffer line.
Advance to the assignment value boundary.
Jump to the final line.
Confirm the first nonblank.
Address one-based column six.

feedback.success: Combined buffer, word, and column destinations.
feedback.why: Each command expressed a different kind of target without touching the text.

provenance.languageRationale: Aligned Python assignments support several meaningful destination types.

activities.title: Move by structure, then row
activities.instruction: Use two word motions, move down, then use W to reach the final WORD boundary.

commandGroups.explanation: Reach the api word after the dot.
Move to the next logical line.
Move from web to the secondary WORD.

hints: Start with a counted small-word motion.
After j, uppercase W treats the dotted token as one WORD.

feedback.success: Mixed lexical and row movement.
feedback.why: The motions matched the token structure before and after the line change.

provenance.languageRationale: Parallel dotted properties provide stable word positions across rows.

activities.title: Return to top and choose a WORD
activities.instruction: Jump to the first line, normalize to first text, then reach `ready` with W.

commandGroups.explanation: Jump to the first buffer line.
Land on its first nonblank.
Treat north-zone as one WORD and reach ready.

hints: Use an absolute buffer jump first.

feedback.success: Reached the top row's status directly.
feedback.why: gg chose the row and W chose the whitespace-delimited token.

provenance.languageRationale: Hyphenated zone names make uppercase WORD movement the natural choice.

activities.title: Reach a precise edge on the last line
activities.instruction: Jump to the last line, normalize to its first text, move two word groups, then step back to the prior word end.

commandGroups.explanation: Jump to the last buffer line.
Normalize to first text.
Move across two small-word groups.
Return to the prior small-word end.

hints: Choose the row before the word edge.

feedback.success: Reached the exact edge on the final line.
feedback.why: Absolute, landmark, forward-word, and reverse-end motions composed without editing.

provenance.languageRationale: Parallel dotted assignments support a precise mixed-motion destination.

activities.title: Choose the meaningful line end
activities.prompt: A line has trailing spaces. Which motion reaches its last nonblank character?
activities.explanation: g_ targets the last nonblank character; $ targets the physical final character, including trailing whitespace.

activities.title: Move by intent, not repeated taps
activities.body: You can now target nearby characters, lexical boundaries, line landmarks, buffer lines, and wrapped display rows without changing text.
takeaways: Choose lowercase word motions when punctuation matters and uppercase WORD motions when whitespace matters.
Use gg, G, and counted G for absolute lines.
Use gj and gk only when you mean visible wrapped rows.

reference.purpose: Move left, down, up, or right without editing.
notes: Prefix a motion with a count to repeat it.
Vertical motions preserve a preferred column where possible.

reference.purpose: Reach column zero, first text, physical end, last nonblank, or a requested column.
notes: $ and g_ differ when trailing whitespace exists.

reference.purpose: Move to the next word or WORD boundary.
notes: Lowercase word movement recognizes punctuation groups.
Uppercase WORD movement uses whitespace boundaries.

reference.command: e / E / b / B / ge / gE
reference.purpose: Reach forward ends, backward starts, or backward ends.
notes: ge and gE are g-prefixed reverse-end motions.

reference.purpose: Reach the first, last, or requested one-based buffer line.
notes: These motions land on the first nonblank character.
A count before G is a line address.

reference.purpose: Move down or up by wrapped display rows.
notes: j and k continue to move by newline-separated logical lines.
The visible destination depends on wrapping and display width.

coverage.concept: h j k l and counts
e E b B ge gE
